primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Dent disease type 1 due to CLCN5 loss
mechanism: ClC-5, encoded by CLCN5, is a chloride/proton exchanger localized to proximal-tubule endosomes. Loss of ClC-5 disrupts endosomal ion handling/acidification and receptor-mediated endocytosis of filtered low-molecular-weight proteins, producing low-molecular-weight proteinuria with hypercalciuria, nephrocalcinosis, and progressive kidney disease.
vignette: An 8-year-old boy has recurrent nephrolithiasis and poor growth. Urinalysis shows marked low-molecular-weight proteinuria despite only mild albuminuria. He also has hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis. His maternal uncle had similar kidney disease. Genetic testing identifies a hemizygous pathogenic variant in CLCN5.
lead: Which of the following proximal-tubule defects most directly explains this patient's proteinuria?
correct: Impaired acidification and receptor-mediated endocytosis within subapical proximal-tubule endosomes
distractors: Failure of lysosomal cystine export with intracellular cystine crystal accumulation
Loss of apical sodium-glucose cotransport causing selective glucosuria
Failure of basolateral bicarbonate exit causing isolated proximal renal tubular acidosis
Loss of the apical cystine/dibasic amino-acid transporter causing cystinuria
distractor_notes: CTNS/cystinosin deficiency causes nephropathic cystinosis with generalized Fanconi syndrome and corneal cystine crystals, a distinct disorder from CLCN5-related Dent disease.
SGLT defects cause renal glucosuria; they do not explain low-molecular-weight proteinuria, hypercalciuria, nephrocalcinosis, and X-linked inheritance.
A bicarbonate-transport defect can cause proximal renal tubular acidosis but would not selectively impair endocytic reabsorption of filtered low-molecular-weight proteins.
Cystinuria is an apical amino-acid transport defect that causes cystine stones but not the characteristic low-molecular-weight proteinuria of Dent disease.
key_expl: Dent disease type 1 is caused by pathogenic CLCN5 variants. ClC-5 is a chloride/proton exchanger in subapical endosomes of proximal tubular cells, where it contributes to normal endosomal ion handling and acidification. Dysfunction impairs receptor-mediated endocytosis/reabsorption of filtered low-molecular-weight proteins, explaining the characteristic proteinuria; hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis are common associated features.
objective: Explain low-molecular-weight proteinuria in Dent disease as a consequence of CLCN5/ClC-5-dependent proximal-tubule endosomal dysfunction and impaired receptor-mediated endocytosis.
